passages.text: The elder, To the beloved Gaius, whom I love in the truth: Beloved, I pray that in every way you may prosper and enjoy good health, as your soul also prospers.
passages.sermon:
The elder writes this letter.
The elder writes to Gaius.
Gaius is beloved.
The elder loves Gaius in the truth.
The elder calls Gaius "beloved."
The elder prays for Gaius.
The elder prays that Gaius may prosper in every way.
The elder prays that Gaius may have good health.
The elder knows that Gaius’s soul prospers.
The elder prays that Gaius’s life and health will prosper as his soul prospers.
passages.original: Ὁ πρεσβύτερος Γαΐῳ τῷ ἀγαπητῷ ὃν ἐγὼ ἀγαπῶ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ Ἀγαπητέ περὶ πάντων εὔχομαί σε εὐοδοῦσθαι καὶ ὑγιαίνειν καθὼς εὐοδοῦταί σου ἡ ψυχή

passages.text: For I was overjoyed when the brothers came and testified about your devotion to the truth, in which you continue to walk.
passages.sermon:
I am the elder.
I write to Gaius.
Gaius is beloved.
I love Gaius in the truth.
Brothers came to me.
These brothers spoke about you, Gaius.
They testified about your devotion to the truth.
You continue to walk in the truth.
I was very glad because of this.
passages.original: ἐχάρην γὰρ λίαν ἐρχομένων ἀδελφῶν καὶ μαρτυρούντων σου τῇ ἀληθείᾳ καθὼς σὺ ἐν ἀληθείᾳ περιπατεῖς

passages.text: I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in the truth.
passages.sermon:
I am the elder.
\r\nI have children in the faith.
\r\nMy children walk in the truth.
\r\nI hear about my children walking in the truth.
\r\nThis gives me the greatest joy.
\r\nNo other joy is greater for me.
passages.original: μειζοτέραν τούτων οὐκ ἔχω χαράν ἵνα ἀκούω τὰ ἐμὰ τέκνα ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ περιπατοῦντα

passages.text: Beloved, you are faithful in what you are doing for the brothers, and especially since they are strangers to you.
passages.sermon:
Beloved, I speak to you.
You act with faithfulness.
You do good works for the brothers.
These brothers are strangers to you.
You remain faithful even to those you do not know.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητέ πιστὸν ποιεῖς ὃ ἐὰν ἐργάσῃ εἰς τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τοῦτο ξένους

passages.text: They have testified to the church about your love. You will do well to send them on their way in a manner worthy of God.
passages.sermon:
The brothers spoke to the church about your love.
They told the church how you showed love.
You should send these brothers on their way.
Send them in a way that honors God.
This will be good for you to do.
passages.original: οἳ ἐμαρτύρησάν σου τῇ ἀγάπῃ ἐνώπιον ἐκκλησίας οὓς καλῶς ποιήσεις προπέμψας ἀξίως τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: For they went out on behalf of the Name, accepting nothing from the Gentiles.
passages.sermon:
These men went out to serve Jesus Christ.
They acted for the sake of His Name.
They did not accept any help from non-believers.
They received nothing from the Gentiles.
passages.original: ὑπὲρ γὰρ τοῦ Ὀνόματος ἐξῆλθον μηδὲν λαμβάνοντες ἀπὸ τῶν ἐθνικῶν

passages.text: Therefore we ought to support such men, so that we may be fellow workers for the truth.
passages.sermon:
We are Christians.
We have a duty.
We ought to support people like these faithful workers.
When we support them, we become fellow workers for the truth.
passages.original: ἡμεῖς οὖν ὀφείλομεν ὑπολαμβάνειν τοὺς τοιούτους ἵνα συνεργοὶ γινώμεθα τῇ ἀληθείᾳ

passages.text: I have written to the church about this, but Diotrephes, who loves to be first, will not accept our instruction.
passages.sermon:
I wrote a letter to the church.
Diotrephes is one of them.
Diotrephes loves to be first.
Diotrephes will not accept us.
Diotrephes will not accept our instruction.
passages.original: Ἔγραψά τι τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ ἀλλ’ ὁ φιλοπρωτεύων αὐτῶν Διοτρεφὴς οὐκ ἐπιδέχεται ἡμᾶς

passages.text: So if I come, I will call attention to his malicious slander against us. And unsatisfied with that, he refuses to welcome the brothers and forbids those who want to do so, even putting them out of the church.
passages.sermon:
Diotrephes is a man who loves to be first among the church.
He does not accept our instruction.
If I come, I will remind everyone of what he does.
He speaks evil words against us.
He is not satisfied with only this.
He does not welcome the brothers.
He stops others who want to welcome them.
He puts those people out of the church.
passages.original: διὰ τοῦτο ἐὰν ἔλθω ὑπομνήσω αὐτοῦ τὰ ἔργα ἃ ποιεῖ λόγοις πονηροῖς φλυαρῶν ἡμᾶς καὶ μὴ ἀρκούμενος ἐπὶ τούτοις οὔτε αὐτὸς ἐπιδέχεται τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς καὶ τοὺς βουλομένους κωλύει καὶ ἐκ τῆς ἐκκλησίας ἐκβάλλει

passages.text: Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. The one who does good is of God; the one who does evil has not seen God.
passages.sermon:
I speak to you, beloved.
Do not copy what is evil.
Copy what is good.
A person who does good comes from God.
A person who does evil has not seen God.
passages.original: Ἀγαπητέ μὴ μιμοῦ τὸ κακὸν ἀλλὰ τὸ ἀγαθόν ὁ ἀγαθοποιῶν ἐκ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ὁ κακοποιῶν οὐχ ἑώρακεν τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: Demetrius has received a good testimony from everyone, and from the truth itself. We also testify for him, and you know that our testimony is true.
passages.sermon:
Demetrius is a Christian brother.
Everyone speaks well of Demetrius.
The truth itself supports Demetrius.
We also speak well of Demetrius.
You know our testimony is true.
passages.original: Δημητρίῳ μεμαρτύρηται ὑπὸ πάντων καὶ ὑπὸ αὐτῆς τῆς ἀληθείας καὶ ἡμεῖς δὲ μαρτυροῦμεν καὶ οἶδας ὅτι ἡ μαρτυρία ἡμῶν ἀληθής ἐστιν

passages.text: I have many things to write to you, but I would prefer not to do so with pen and ink.
passages.sermon: I have many things to write to you.\r\nI do not want to write them with pen and ink.\r\n
passages.original: Πολλὰ εἶχον γράψαι σοι ἀλλ’ οὐ θέλω διὰ μέλανος καὶ καλάμου σοι γράφειν

passages.text: Instead, I hope to see you soon and speak with you face to face. Peace to you. The friends here send you greetings. Greet each of our friends there by name.
passages.sermon:
I hope to see you soon.
I want to speak with you face to face.
I pray for peace for you.
The friends here greet you.
Greet each of our friends there by name.
passages.original: ἐλπίζω δὲ εὐθέως σε ἰδεῖν καὶ στόμα πρὸς στόμα λαλήσομεν Εἰρήνη σοι Ἀσπάζονταί σε οἱ φίλοι Ἀσπάζου τοὺς φίλους κατ’ ὄνομα
